setting.title: The Conductor's Watch
setting.premise: Cora Delacroix chartered a restored sleeper train for a long weekend to mark her retirement, and invited five guests aboard. On Saturday morning her late father's railroad pocket watch is gone from its little oak box in the observation car.
setting.background: The Juniper Limited is a restored 1950s steam train: the locomotive, then the baggage car, the sleeper car, the dining car and, at the very back, the observation car. To get from one car to the next you walk through the vestibules between them. The baggage car holds everyone's suitcases, old mail-sorting cubbies and a bicycle rack; it sits right behind the steam engine, so its floor is always gritty with coal soot. The sleeper car has a corridor down one side, six compartments, and the washroom at the baggage-car end. Compartment 1, nearest the dining car, is Cora's; Lottie and her granddaughter Kit share compartment 2, with bunks; Ambrose has 3, Signe 4 and Dez 5, and 6 holds the spare linen. The dining car has four tables and a little galley at one end, where Dez cooks for everyone. The observation car is a lounge with armchairs, a small bar, big curved windows, a shelf under the rear window and a brass-railed open platform off the back. Each car has its own Wi-Fi access point; the signal doesn't reach far beyond the train. Each night the train is parked on the siding at Pine Hollow station, a little mountain halt by a lake: one platform, a water tower and a station building that's locked at night. The village is a ten-minute walk down the road. The two-man crew sleeps at the inn in the village from about 9pm to 7am, so at night only the six guests are aboard. Friday: everyone boarded at Harlow Junction at 2pm, the train climbed into the mountains and was parked at Pine Hollow by 6, and Dez served dinner in the dining car at 7. At 10pm everyone gathered in the observation car for Cora's toast. She wound her father's watch, set it in its open oak box on the shelf under the rear window to keep train time for the weekend, and announced that on Monday, at the end of the line, she would give it to the railway museum at Carver's Gap. Saturday and Sunday the train runs a scenic loop up the mountain and back to the siding by evening; Monday morning it runs down to Carver's Gap. The watch belonged to Cora and Lottie's father, Augie Delacroix, who carried it for forty years as a conductor on this very line: gold-filled and open-faced, with a white enamel dial, black numerals, a little locomotive engraved on the back of the case and a brass chain. Its oak box is lined with green felt.
setting.missingItem: Cora's late father's railroad pocket watch

guests.name: Cora Delacroix
guests.role: the host, a conductor on this line for thirty-three years until her retirement last month
guests.voice: Warm and brisk, with a conductor's habits: full sentences with proper capitals, railway talk ('right on schedule', 'end of the line', 'all aboard'), exclamation marks when she's pleased, and a 🚂 now and then, never more than one and never alongside another emoji.

topics.description: where Cora was and when she went to bed on Friday night, the night the watch vanished

variants.text: Tucked up in compartment 1 by half past ten, out like a lamp until 6:30. Thirty years of early shifts, detective.
Bed at 10:30 on Friday, and I slept straight through until half past six. I never heard a thing.

topics.description: where Cora was on Saturday night and whether she got up in the night

variants.text: Tonight? Bed early, I hope. Ask me in the morning!
Saturday night's still ahead of us. Ask me tomorrow.
I tossed and turned, and at ten past two I gave up and warmed some milk in the galley. Back in bed by half past.
Couldn't sleep for worrying. I was in the galley at 2:10 warming milk, then back to bed.

topics.description: where Cora was on Sunday night, the last night aboard

variants.text: Sunday night hasn't happened yet, detective! Ask me Monday.
Ask me tomorrow, at the end of the line.
After our last dinner I went straight to bed, about ten. Slept like a stone, for once.
Bed at ten on Sunday. I was worn out. I never stirred.

topics.description: the missing pocket watch itself, where Cora kept it and when she found it gone

variants.text: I wound it at the 10pm toast and set it in its oak box on the shelf under the rear window. At seven on Saturday, when I went to wind it, the box was empty.
In its little oak box in the observation car, from the toast at ten. Seven o'clock Saturday morning I went to wind it, like Dad always did, and it was gone.

topics.description: Cora's late father Augie, his forty years as a conductor, and the watch's history

variants.text: Dad carried that watch on this very line for forty years. Every train he ever punched a ticket on ran to it. 🚂
Augie Delacroix. Best conductor the line ever had, and he'd tell you so himself. He wound that watch at seven every morning of his life.

topics.description: whether Cora and Lottie's father promised the watch to Lottie

variants.text: Lottie's said since we were girls that Dad promised it to her. He never did. He promised it to the line.
Oh, that old story. Lottie has always said Dad promised her the watch. I've never once heard him say it.

topics.description: Cora's plan to give the watch to the railway museum at Carver's Gap on Monday

variants.text: The museum at Carver's Gap has a whole wall for the conductors of this line. Dad's watch belongs there, where everyone can see it.
I'd so wanted to put it in the curator's hands myself on Monday. End of the line, end of an era. Now look.

topics.description: Lottie, Cora's younger sister, and how she's taken the museum news

variants.text: My little sister. Bless her, she grumbled all through Friday's dinner about Dad's watch going to a museum. She'll come round.
Lottie? She wasn't happy about the museum, I'll tell you that. Muttered about it from soup to pudding on Friday.

topics.description: Ambrose, the retired engine driver who fired for Cora's father, and his grudge about the watch

variants.text: Ambrose claims Dad won that watch off his grandfather in a card game in '58, so it's 'rightfully a Teague watch'. And he stayed behind with it after the toast. I hate to think it.
Ambrose has gone on for years about a card game in 1958, says the watch is really his family's. He sat on alone in the observation car after we all left on Friday.

topics.description: Signe, Cora's neighbour and best friend, and her big picnic basket

variants.text: Signe's my oldest friend. She brought an enormous picnic basket aboard and won't let it out of her sight. Shortbread, I expect!
Signe and I have been neighbours for thirty years. Quiet as a mouse, sharp as a tack.

topics.description: Dez, Cora's godson, the chef cooking in the galley

variants.text: My godson! He's cooking for the whole trip in that tiny galley. The man's a miracle with a two-ring stove.
Dez has fed us like royalty all weekend. Loves a bit of gossip, mind you.

topics.description: Kit, Lottie's granddaughter, the youngest aboard

variants.text: Lottie's granddaughter. Sweet girl, glued to her phone, and jumpy as a cricket all weekend.
Kit's at college now, can you believe it. She's been on edge since Saturday, poor thing.

topics.description: Friday evening from dinner to the toast: Cora's speech, and who stayed behind afterward

variants.text: Dinner at seven, then the toast at ten in the observation car. I wound the watch and set it in its box. Afterwards everyone drifted off except Ambrose, who stayed on with a whiskey.
At the 10pm toast I set Dad's watch in its box to keep train time. Ambrose stayed behind on his own when the rest of us left.

topics.description: who Cora thinks took the watch and why

variants.text: I hate to say it. Ambrose has always said the watch is rightfully his family's, from that card game in '58. But I can't believe it of him.
If you're asking who wanted it, Ambrose has said for years it's a Teague watch by rights. I'd rather it were anyone else.

topics.description: any noises, lights or people Cora noticed during Friday night

variants.text: Not a thing, I'm afraid. I sleep like a log on a train. Always have.
I heard nothing at all on Friday night. The rocking puts me straight out, even parked.

topics.description: anything Cora noticed or anything that happened during Saturday night

variants.text: Nothing's happened yet tonight, detective.
Ask me in the morning.
I was up in the galley at ten past two warming milk. The whole train was quiet as a church.
Nobody about when I warmed my milk at 2:10, not a soul.

topics.description: anything Cora noticed or anything that happened during Sunday night

variants.text: Sunday night's still to come.
Ask me tomorrow, dear.
I slept through it all. Signe says someone ran the tap half the night, but I never heard it.
Didn't hear a thing. I was dead to the world from ten.

topics.description: the Juniper Limited itself, the cars, the crew and where it runs

variants.text: Isn't she lovely? 1952 sleeper, steam all the way. The crew sleep at the inn in the village, so at night she's all ours. 🚂
The Juniper Limited! I chartered her for my retirement. Every night she sits on the siding at Pine Hollow, and Monday she runs down to Carver's Gap.

topics.description: the railway's rules aboard: no pets, no smoking, keep off the tracks

variants.text: Rules are rules, even on a charter. No pets, no smoking, and nobody on the tracks at night. Dad would haunt me.
The railway's very strict: no animals aboard, no exceptions. I signed the form myself.

topics.description: Cora's own phone and what the Wi-Fi log shows of it

variants.text: My phone sits on the shelf in my compartment all night. If the log says I wandered, it was to the galley for milk.
I'm not much for phones. Mine goes where I go, I suppose.
Me? Detective, it's my father's watch. I'd sooner lose my right arm.
I chartered a whole train to give that watch a proper send-off. Why on earth would I steal it from myself?

dodges: I couldn't tell you, I'm afraid.
Now that's one for someone else, dear.
Ask Dez, he hears everything in that galley.
I wasn't paying attention to that, I'm sorry.
greetings: Good morning, detective! Right on schedule.
dictionary.goodnight: Lights out for me, detective. We'll pick it up in the morning. 🚂

guests.name: Lottie Ambler
guests.role: Cora's younger sister, Kit's grandmother, and the family's champion gossip
guests.voice: Cosy and conspiratorial. Calls everyone 'pet' or 'dear', loves 'between you and me' and a trailing '...', full sentences with proper capitals, and a 🤫 when she's passing on something she shouldn't, never more than one.

topics.description: where Lottie was and when she slept on Friday night, the night the watch vanished

variants.text: In my bunk in compartment 2, pet, asleep by eleven and never stirred till morning. My hips don't do midnight wanders.
Asleep by eleven on Friday, dear, and I didn't get up once. Kit will tell you, I snore like a goods train.

topics.description: where Lottie was on Saturday night and what she and Kit did in their compartment

variants.text: Tonight? A hand of cards with Kit and an early night, I expect. Ask me tomorrow, pet.
Ask me in the morning, dear.
Kit and I just played gin rummy in our compartment, pet. We never said a word about Friday, why would we?
Cards with Kit, that's all. Gin rummy till half ten. Friday never came up, dear, not once.

topics.description: where Lottie was on Sunday night and whether she got up

variants.text: Sunday hasn't happened yet, pet!
Ask me Monday, dear.
Asleep by half past ten, pet, and not a peep out of me till morning.
Bed at half ten on Sunday and I slept right through, dear. Didn't get up once.

topics.description: the missing pocket watch and where Lottie last saw it

variants.text: Cora wound it at the toast at ten and popped it in its little box on the shelf. That's the last I saw of it, pet.
In its box in the observation car, from the ten o'clock toast. Dad's old watch... Such a shame.

topics.description: how Lottie feels about Cora giving their father's watch to the railway museum

variants.text: Oh, I think it's lovely, pet. Dad behind glass for everyone to see. I'm thrilled for Cora, truly.
The museum? I'm glad, dear. It's where Dad would want it. I said so to Cora myself.

topics.description: the baggage car up front, the luggage and the soot, and whether Lottie has been in it

variants.text: That filthy place? I haven't set foot in it since we boarded on Friday, pet. The crew loaded my case.
Not since Friday afternoon, dear. Soot everywhere, it'd ruin my good cardigan.

topics.description: Lottie's pink slippers and whether they've been anywhere grubby

variants.text: My slippers? Pink, fluffy and they've never been near that grubby baggage car, pet. Why ever do you ask?
What an odd question, dear. My slippers have never been in the baggage car. I haven't been in it since Friday afternoon.

topics.description: Lottie's own phone and what the Wi-Fi log shows it doing at night

variants.text: Oh, I don't understand that log business, pet. My phone does as it pleases.
Kit set it up for me. Couldn't tell you where it goes at night, dear.

topics.description: Lottie and Cora's father Augie and the watch's history

variants.text: Dad wound that watch at seven every morning, and when I was little he'd let me hold it while he did. Happy days...
Augie Delacroix, conductor, forty years on this line. Cora was his shadow. I was his little helper.

topics.description: Cora, Lottie's older sister and the host

variants.text: My big sister. Bossy since 1960, between you and me, but a heart of gold.
Cora runs this trip like a timetable, pet. Always has.

topics.description: Kit, Lottie's granddaughter, who shares her compartment

variants.text: My Kit's a good girl. Ask her anything, pet, she was right there in the top bunk.
My granddaughter. Sweet as anything, sleeps like the dead. Don't you go upsetting her.

topics.description: Ambrose, the grumpy old engine driver, and his card-game grudge

variants.text: Between you and me, pet, Ambrose says Dad won that watch off his grandfather in a card game in '58. And who stayed behind with it after the toast? Ambrose. 🤫
Ambrose has always said it's rightfully a Teague watch, from some card game in 1958. And he sat on alone with it after the toast, dear. I'm only saying.

topics.description: Signe, Cora's best friend, and the picnic basket she guards

variants.text: Now, Signe and her picnic basket... Dez says he heard it whimper on Saturday, pet. Whimper! 🤫
Ask Signe what's in that basket, dear. Dez heard a whimper come out of it on Saturday.

topics.description: Dez, Cora's godson the chef

variants.text: Lovely boy, Dez. Makes a beautiful lemon cake, and he does love a natter.
Dez? A sweetheart. In and out of that galley at all hours, mind you.

topics.description: what Lottie did on Friday evening between the toast and bed

variants.text: After the toast Kit and I went back to our compartment, and I was asleep by eleven, pet.
We left the toast and went to bed, dear. Asleep by eleven, me.

topics.description: who Lottie thinks took the watch and why

variants.text: Well, I wouldn't like to say... but Ambrose thinks it's his family's watch, and he was alone with it after the toast. 🤫
Between you and me, pet? Ambrose. Card game in '58, says the watch should be his, and he stayed behind with it on Friday.

topics.description: any noises, lights or people Lottie noticed during Friday night

variants.text: Not a peep, pet. I was sound asleep by eleven.
Nothing, dear. Asleep by eleven and I never woke.

topics.description: anything Lottie noticed or anything that happened during Saturday night

variants.text: Nothing's happened yet, pet.
We'll see, dear. Ask me in the morning.
Only Cora clanking about the galley at ten past two, so I'm told. Poor love can't sleep.
Cora was up warming milk at 2:10, dear. That's all the excitement I know of.

topics.description: anything Lottie noticed or anything that happened during Sunday night, including the running tap

variants.text: Sunday's still to come, pet.
Ask me Monday, dear.
A tap running? I was asleep by half ten, pet. Ambrose is up all hours, ask him.
Slept like a log from half past ten, dear. Didn't hear any tap.

topics.description: Lottie's knitting and how she passes the time aboard

variants.text: A scarf for Kit, pet. Green, her favourite. I'll have it done by Carver's Gap.
Knitting and a good natter, dear, that's my idea of a holiday.
Me? Steal from my own sister? Honestly, pet. Ask Ambrose about his grandfather's card game.
I'll pretend you didn't say that, dear. If anyone thinks that watch is theirs by rights, it's Ambrose. Card game, 1958.
How dare you, pet. Ask Ambrose about his card game, and while you're at it ask Signe why her basket whimpers.
Me?! Ambrose says the watch is rightfully his, and Dez heard Signe's basket whimper. Look there, dear.

dodges: You'd have to ask someone else, dear.
That's not for me to say...
No idea, dear. Not a clue.
Ooh, I don't know. Ask Dez, he hears everything.
greetings: Hello, dear. Come for a natter?
dictionary.goodnight: I'm off to my bunk, pet. Ask me in the morning.

guests.name: Ambrose Teague
guests.role: a retired engine driver who fired for Cora's father on this line in the sixties
guests.voice: Gruff and clipped. Short sentences, full stops, no emoji, the odd 'hmph', grumbles about how things were done in the old days.

topics.description: where Ambrose was and when he went to bed on Friday night, after he sat up with the watch

variants.text: Left the observation car at quarter past eleven. Watch was in its box, I checked the time on it. Went to my compartment and stayed there.
Quarter past eleven, I went to bed. The watch was still there. I didn't come out again till morning.

topics.description: where Ambrose was on Saturday night

variants.text: Night's not over. Ask me tomorrow.
Tomorrow.
Observation car from quarter past ten to five past eleven. A whiskey and the stars. Then bed.
Sat up in the observation car, 10:15 to 11:05. Then I turned in.

topics.description: where Ambrose was on Sunday night

variants.text: It's not Sunday night yet.
Ask me Monday.
Observation car, twenty to eleven till ten to midnight. Nobody came through. Then bed.
I sat in the observation car from 10:40 to 11:50. Not a soul came by.

topics.description: the missing pocket watch and when Ambrose last saw it

variants.text: Cora put it in the box at the toast at ten. Still there at quarter past eleven when I left. I checked the time on it.
In its box from ten o'clock. It was there at 11:15 when I went to bed. Kept good time, too.

topics.description: Ambrose's claim that Cora's father won the watch from his grandfather in a card game

variants.text: Augie Delacroix won that watch off my grandfather in a card game in 1958. Rightfully it's a Teague watch. I've never pretended otherwise.
Card game, 1958. My grandfather's watch, Augie's winnings. Everyone knows I think it's ours.

topics.description: whether Ambrose went back to the observation car later on Friday night, after he'd gone to bed

variants.text: Went back? No. I was in my compartment from quarter past eleven.
I didn't leave my compartment after 11:15. Who says otherwise?

topics.description: Cora's plan to give the watch to the museum at Carver's Gap

variants.text: A museum. Behind glass with a typed card. A watch is meant to be wound.
Hmph. Carver's Gap museum. They'll spell Augie's name wrong, you watch.

topics.description: Ambrose's own phone and what the Wi-Fi log shows of it

variants.text: Phone's in my pocket. Don't know what the router thinks it's doing.
I don't hold with Wi-Fi logs. Ask the machine.

topics.description: Cora, the host, Augie's daughter

variants.text: Good conductor. Better than her father, and don't tell her I said so.
Cora runs a tight train. Always did.

topics.description: Lottie, Cora's sister, and what she said about the watch on Friday

variants.text: Lottie stopped me at the door at twenty to eleven on Friday. Said 'Dad promised that watch to me' and called the museum a crime. She wasn't joking.
At 10:40 Friday Lottie told me her father promised her that watch. Called it a crime to put it behind glass.

topics.description: Signe, Cora's quiet neighbour

variants.text: Signe keeps herself to herself. Good.
Quiet woman. Reads. Doesn't natter. I like her.

topics.description: Dez, the chef in the galley

variants.text: Boy can cook. Talks too much.
Dez's eggs are right. His mouth runs on.

topics.description: Kit, Lottie's granddaughter

variants.text: The girl's on her phone more than she's off it. Jumpy, too.
Kit. Nervous as a cat all weekend.

topics.description: Friday evening after the toast, when Ambrose sat on alone with the watch

variants.text: Everyone cleared off after the toast. I stayed on with a whiskey. The watch was in its box when I left at quarter past eleven.
Sat alone in the observation car after the toast. One whiskey. Left at 11:15 and the watch was still there.

topics.description: who Ambrose thinks took the watch and why

variants.text: Ask Lottie. Twenty to eleven on Friday she told me her father promised it to her. People don't say that for nothing.
Lottie. She told me at 10:40 Friday that watch was promised to her. Or the girl, out all hours. Not me.

topics.description: any noises, lights or people Ambrose noticed during Friday night

variants.text: Heard nothing. I was in my bunk from quarter past eleven.
Nothing. I was in my compartment from 11:15 and I sleep sound.

topics.description: anything Ambrose noticed or anything that happened during Saturday night

variants.text: Nothing yet.
Ask me tomorrow.
Quiet night. Whispering next door in compartment 2 about ten. None of my business.
Nothing worth telling.

topics.description: anything Ambrose noticed or anything that happened during Sunday night, including the running tap

variants.text: Night's not here yet.
Monday.
I was at the back of the train in the observation car, 10:40 to 11:50. No tap, nobody came through.
Couldn't hear a washroom from the observation car. I was there till ten to midnight. Nobody passed me.

topics.description: Ambrose's years driving steam on this line and the locomotive

variants.text: Drove this line twenty-two years. They're firing her wrong on the grade. Too much coal, too soon.
I fired for Augie in '64. Steam was steam then. Now it's a day out.

topics.description: the baggage car behind the engine

variants.text: Sooty. Always was. Engine's right in front of it.
Baggage car's filthy. You walk through there, you carry it out on your feet.
All right. I went back at half past one. One last look at my grandfather's watch. The box was already empty. I said nothing because I knew how it'd look.
Fine. Half one, I went back to the observation car to see it one more time. Box was empty. I kept quiet. Who'd believe me?

guests.name: Signe Halvorsen
guests.role: Cora's next-door neighbour and best friend of thirty years, a retired school librarian
guests.voice: Precise and sparing. Complete sentences, perfect punctuation, no emoji, rarely more than two sentences, answers exactly what was asked and not a word more.

topics.description: where Signe was on Friday night and whether she left her compartment or the train

variants.text: In compartment 4 from eleven. I did not leave the train.
I went to bed at eleven. I have not stepped off this train at night.

topics.description: where Signe was on Saturday night

variants.text: Ask me tomorrow.
The night is not over.
In my compartment, reading. I did not leave the train.
Compartment 4, all night. I have not been off the train at night.

topics.description: where Signe was on Sunday night

variants.text: Ask me on Monday.
Sunday has not happened yet.
In my compartment. I did not leave the train.
Reading in compartment 4. I have not set foot off the train at night all weekend.

topics.description: the missing pocket watch and where Signe last saw it

variants.text: Cora set it in its box on the shelf at the toast at ten. I did not see it again.
In the oak box in the observation car, from ten o'clock on Friday.

topics.description: Signe's big picnic basket and what's inside it

topics.description: Signe's own phone and what the Wi-Fi log shows it doing

variants.text: I do not follow what the log shows. My phone is in my cardigan pocket.

topics.description: Cora, the host and Signe's best friend

topics.description: Lottie, Cora's sister, and the slippers she leaves outside compartment 2

Her slippers sit outside her door. The soles were black with soot this morning, the baggage car kind.

variants.text: Ambrose stayed on alone in the observation car after the toast. Make of that what you will.

topics.description: Dez, Cora's godson the chef

topics.description: Kit, Lottie's granddaughter

topics.description: Cora's plan to give the watch to the museum, and how people took it

topics.description: Dez's own phone and what the Wi-Fi log shows of it

topics.description: Cora, Dez's godmother and the host

topics.description: Ambrose, the grumpy old engine driver with the card-game grudge

topics.description: Signe, Cora's quiet best friend, and the picnic basket that whimpers

topics.description: Kit, Lottie's granddaughter

variants.text: Sweet kid. Jumpy as anything this weekend, mind you.

topics.description: what Dez did on Friday evening after dinner and the toast

topics.description: who Dez thinks took the watch and why

variants.text: Honestly? Either Ambrose, who thinks it's his granddad's watch, or Signe, whose picnic basket whimpers. I'm not making that up.

topics.description: anything Dez noticed during Friday night on his trip to the galley

variants.text: Only thing: at 12:35 the watch was still in its box, I saw it through the door. So whoever took it went in after that.

topics.description: anything Dez noticed or overheard during Saturday night

variants.text: Nothing yet, ask me tomorrow!

topics.description: anything Dez noticed or anything that happened during Sunday night

variants.text: Ask me tomorrow!

topics.description: the meals Dez has cooked aboard and what's on the menu

variants.text: Friday was trout with brown butter, Saturday lemon cake for the picnic. Tonight? Surprise.

topics.description: the baggage car and the supplies Dez keeps there

Me?! I was in the galley at 12:35 feeding my starter and the watch was RIGHT THERE in its box. Back in bed by 12:41. Why would I tell you that if I'd nicked it 😅

timeline.text: Cora's toast in the observation car. She winds her father's watch and sets it in its oak box.
Cora goes to bed.
Leaving the toast, Lottie tells Ambrose their father promised her the watch. She and Kit go to compartment 2. Ambrose stays on with a whiskey.
Ambrose checks the time on the watch, still in its box, and goes to bed.
Dez finishes in the galley and goes to bed.
Signe carries Pickle, her smuggled dachshund, out to the platform.
Kit slips off the train to meet her girlfriend in the village. Signe sees her go. Lottie, wide awake in the bottom bunk, hears her too.
Dez feeds his sourdough starter in the galley and sees the watch through the observation car door.
Lottie walks back through the dining car to the observation car.
Lottie takes the watch.
Lottie pads up the sleeper corridor, past Signe, to the baggage car, and hides the watch in a mail cubby. Coal soot gets on her slippers.
Lottie is back in her bunk.
Ambrose creeps back for one last look at the watch and finds the box empty. He tells no one.
Kit is back aboard.
Cora goes to wind the watch and finds the box empty. Signe notices soot on the soles of the slippers outside compartment 2.
Lottie tells Kit she knows Kit snuck out, and asks her to say Lottie never left her bunk on Friday. In return, Kit's mother never hears about it. Dez overhears through the door.
Ambrose sits up in the observation car until 11:05.
Dez bakes for Sunday until half past midnight.
Signe takes Pickle out to the platform again. Kit hears him yap.
Cora can't sleep and warms some milk in the galley.
Kit slips off to say goodbye to Tamsin.
Ambrose sits in the observation car until 11:50.
Pickle's last walk on the platform.
Lottie scrubs the soot off her slippers in the washroom. Signe hears the tap running.
Kit, just back aboard, sees Lottie come out of the washroom carrying her dripping slippers.
Lottie fetches the watch from the mail cubby and packs it in her own suitcase, ready to take home on Monday.
